 affected feeder warrants such a change. The determination shall be made per site by Distribution Protection
Engineering and recorded in the site's interconnection file.

5.5 Settings Governance
All protection settings for the POI recloser, and any changes to upstream feeder recloser settings driven by the
DER interconnection, shall be issued in writing by Distribution Protection Engineering and shall not be altered in
the field without a written revision order.

6. TESTING
6.1 Factory Acceptance
The POI recloser and its control shall be subjected to factory acceptance testing per the manufacturer's standard
test protocol and per IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111, with test records delivered to Alleniom Utilities prior to
shipment.

6.2 Site Acceptance
Prior to placing the DER site in service, the following site acceptance activities shall be performed and witnessed
by Alleniom Utilities:
1. Insulation resistance and dielectric withstand testing of primary and secondary circuits.
2. Current transformer and voltage transformer ratio, polarity, and burden verification.
3. Functional testing of each enabled ANSI device function against its issued setting, including pickup, timing,
and reset.
4. End-to-end trip testing from each protection element through the recloser interrupter.
5. Verification of local and remote (SCADA) control, status, and metering per TCS-02.
6. Verification of synchronism check and reclose-block logic.
7. Verification of visible-break disconnect operation and lockout provisions.

6.3 Commissioning and Cutover
Cutover of the DER site to the distribution system shall not proceed until all §6.2 activities are complete and
accepted in writing by Alleniom Utilities. The site's initial parallel operation shall be observed by the utility system
operator with the POI recloser under active SCADA supervision.

6.4 Periodic Testing
The POI recloser shall be included in the utility's periodic recloser maintenance program. DER-side protective
devices shall be tested by the DER owner on a schedule not to exceed that of comparable utility-owned
equipment, with test records made available to Alleniom Utilities on request.

6.5 Post-Event Testing
Following any operation of the POI recloser attributable to a system disturbance, a DER-side event, or a
mis-operation, Distribution Protection Engineering shall review the event records and direct such retesting or
resetting as it determines appropriate before the site is returned to service.

§1 PURPOSE
This standard establishes the minimum technical and operational requirements for real-time
telemetry and communications between in-scope Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities
and the Alleniom Utilities System Operations Center (SOC). It governs the equipment, data
content, refresh cadence, communications transport, and cybersecurity posture required for a
DER facility to be observed and dispatchable through the utility's Supervisory Control and Data
Acquisition (SCADA) system.
TCS-02 is one component of Alleniom's DER interconnection framework. Its provisions are limited
to telemetry and communications. Requirements for interconnection classification, protective
functions, service agreements, commissioning, and other lifecycle activities are addressed in the
standards and procedures cited by the interconnection standard (DIS-01) and are outside the
scope of this document.

§2 SCOPE
TCS-02 applies to every in-scope DER site as defined by DIS-01 §3 — that is, every DER whose
nameplate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold of 500 kW. Sub-500 kW DER
handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process is outside the scope of this standard.
TCS-02 applies to:
•

a. Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW).

•

b. Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW).

•

c. Aggregated DER facilities recognized as a single site under DIS-01 §3.4, where the
aggregate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold.

•

d. DER commissioned on or after the effective date of this standard, and DER
commissioned before the effective date that undergo material modification, POI relocation, or
capacity change requiring a new interconnection application.

Where a DER site interfaces with the distribution system through a shared point of common
coupling with other generation, the aggregate facility is the object of this standard, and the
aggregate is measured and controlled as a single interconnected entity.

§3 RTU REQUIREMENTS
§3.1 Ownership and installation
Each in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU)
installed at, or immediately adjacent to, the point of interconnection. The RTU shall be procured,
owned, installed, configured, maintained, and — where required — replaced by Alleniom Utilities.
The customer shall provide the physical mounting location, environmental enclosure, station AC
service, and communications entrance conduit specified in the utility's site-specific RTU
installation drawing.
§3.2 Approved models
The utility-owned RTU shall be one of the three models currently used for utility-owned RTU
service: YOT-8963, YOT-8856, or YOT-7963. Substitution is not permitted. A customer power
plant controller (PPC) may use any RTU on the plant side, provided it can communicate with the
utility-owned RTU via DNP3 (§4.2).
§3.3 Functional requirements
Each RTU shall, at minimum:
•

a. Poll the DER facility's generation metering, inverter/PCS gateway, and station
instrumentation at the refresh cadence specified in §6.

•

b. Encode and forward the required data points (§6) to the Alleniom SCADA front-end
processors over an approved communications path (§4).

•

c. Timestamp all values to a common reference (§3.5) and buffer data locally for a minimum
of seventy-two (72) hours in the event of communications loss, with automatic backfill upon
restoration.

•

d. Report communications status, device health, and configuration version to SCADA as
diagnostic points.

•

e. Accept authenticated remote configuration updates and firmware from Alleniom
SCADA/EMS Engineering only.

§3.4 Environmental and station-service requirements
The RTU enclosure shall meet the environmental rating specified in the site-specific installation
drawing. Station AC service to the enclosure shall be provided by the customer through a
dedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply sized for a minimum four (4) hour
outage ride-through, sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages.
§3.5 Time synchronization
The RTU shall discipline its internal clock to an authoritative time source using either GNSS (GPS)
time or the Alleniom SCADA network time reference. All values reported to SCADA shall carry a
timestamp accurate to within ±1 second of UTC.
§3.6 Commissioning and end-to-end verification

Prior to the RTU being accepted as commissioned, Alleniom shall perform an end-to-end
point-to-point test that verifies each required data point (§6) at the SCADA operator display,
exercises any control points released to SCADA, and validates alarm and quality flags.
Commissioning of the RTU is a prerequisite to the telemetry condition stated in §5.

§4 COMMUNICATIONS
§4.1 Communications transport
The RTU shall communicate with Alleniom SCADA over one of the transports approved by
SCADA/EMS Engineering:
•

a. Utility-managed fiber to an Alleniom aggregation node, or

•

b. Utility-provisioned licensed private wireless (point-to-multipoint), or

•

c. Utility-provisioned cellular service on the approved carrier list, using SIM credentials held
by Alleniom.

Customer-owned or shared-use networks are not permitted as the primary telemetry transport.
Where site conditions do not permit any of the transports listed above, the site is not eligible for
interconnection under the DER Program until a suitable transport can be provisioned.
§4.2 SCADA protocol
The RTU shall communicate with SCADA using DNP3 Serial or DNP3 over TCP/IP. Secure
Authentication v5 shall be enabled on the DNP3 link where supported by the RTU. Configuration
parameters — DNP3 addresses, timeouts, unsolicited response classes, integrity poll intervals —
shall follow the site-specific configuration record issued by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
§4.3 Availability
The end-to-end telemetry path (RTU, transport, front-end processor) shall be designed for a
monthly availability of not less than 99.5 percent, measured at the SCADA front-end. Persistent
loss of telemetry constitutes a departure from the site's interconnection basis and shall be
corrected by the customer and utility working together to the extent each owns the affected
equipment.
§4.4 Address and IP management
All IP addresses, DNP3 addresses, VLAN assignments, and routing between the RTU and
Alleniom SCADA are assigned and managed by Alleniom. Customer equipment shall not initiate
connections toward the RTU other than as expressly permitted in the site-specific configuration
record.

§5 TELEMETRY CONDITION FOR PERMISSION TO OPERATE
§5. ≥500 kW requires utility-owned RTU + SCADA telemetry; no PTO without live telemetry.
This requirement applies to all in-scope DER sites, including aggregated facilities under
DIS-01 §3.4.
Live telemetry, for the purposes of §5, means that the RTU installed under §3 is:
•

a. Physically installed, configured, and end-to-end commissioned in accordance with §3.6;

Analog values shall be updated to SCADA at intervals no longer than four (4) seconds using DNP3
Class 1/2 event reporting for point-on-change and Class 0 integrity poll no less frequently than
every sixty (60) seconds. Status points shall be reported by exception on change of state, with an

reported no less frequently than every five (5) minutes.
§6.3 Data quality
Every value delivered to SCADA shall carry a DNP3 quality flag. Values shall be marked online,
restart, communications lost, or over-range as circumstances warrant. Values held constant by the
RTU during communications loss shall not be reported as online upon restoration; they shall be
reported with the communications-lost flag until fresh source values are acquired.
§6.4 Retention
Alleniom retains all telemetry from in-scope DER sites in the historian for a minimum of thirty-six
(36) months at the raw acquisition cadence, and indefinitely at hourly aggregation, for planning,
engineering analysis, and regulatory reporting.

§7 CYBERSECURITY
§7.1 Applicability
The RTU, the communications transport between the RTU and Alleniom SCADA, and any
customer equipment that shares a physical or logical interface with the RTU are subject to this
section. Alleniom-owned assets covered here are administered under Alleniom's cyber-security
program consistent with NIST SP 800-82 and NERC CIP where applicable.
§7.2 Access control
Local and remote access to the RTU is limited to Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering and to
Alleniom-authorized service personnel. Local craft access requires two-factor authentication
against Alleniom's identity system. Passwords, shared secrets, and cryptographic keys are
managed by Alleniom and are not disclosed to the customer, developer, or any third party.
§7.3 Communications security
DNP3 Secure Authentication v5 shall be enabled where supported by the RTU. All
communications traversing any non-utility segment shall be tunneled through an
Alleniom-managed VPN using IPsec (IKEv2) with mutual certificate authentication. Certificates
shall have a maximum validity of thirteen (13) months and are rotated by Alleniom.
§7.4 Firmware, configuration, and change management
RTU firmware and configuration are updated only by Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering, following

The RTU shall log authentication events, configuration changes, communications state transitions,
and firmware operations. Logs are forwarded to Alleniom's centralized log-management system.
Anomalies detected by that system are handled per Alleniom's cyber-security incident response
procedure.

[P8] (Normal): Subject:     Bramwick Commons Solar (1.8 MW AC, Feeder ALN-214) — Supplemental Review Screen Determination (PASSED), Reversal and Supersession of Countersigned Memo IS-BRAM-2025-06-25 (Rev v1, 06/25/2025), and Clearance to ISA Drafting
[P11] (Normal): 1. Project Identification and Subject Feeder Baseline (As of 07/14/2025)
[P12] (Normal): Bramwick Commons Solar LLC submitted an interconnection application for the Bramwick Commons Solar project, a 1.8 MW AC (1,800 kW) pure-export front-of-the-meter solar photovoltaic generating facility proposing to interconnect to Feeder ALN-214 out of Larkspur Ridge Substation (12.47 kV nominal primary voltage). Because the facility's nameplate capacity is ≥ 500 kW and ≤ 2.0 MW, the application falls within the commercial DER Program scope under DIS-01 Rev 4 §3.1 and within the Fast-Track eligibility ceiling under DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.1 and Tariff §12.1. Following failure of the initial fast-track 15%-of-peak-load screen (DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.2(a)), the application was routed to Supplemental Review pursuant to DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.3, Tariff §12.2, and SRP-3 Rev 3 §2.
[P14] (Normal): 2. Review of Countersigned Memo IS-BRAM-2025-06-25 (Rev v1) and Basis for Reversal
[P15] (Normal): In compliance with the Backlog Review Directive (DIR-2025-0627, issued 06/27/2025 by VP Dana Whitcomb), the Regulatory Affairs Tasking Memo (RA-2025-07-01 §3.9, issued 07/01/2025 by Director Harriet Ngoyi), and SRP-3 Rev 3 §7, Interconnection Studies audited Bramwick_Commons_Screening_Memo_v1.docx (Doc no. IS-BRAM-2025-06-25, Rev v1, signed by Priya Ranganathan and countersigned by Meera Vellanki on 06/25/2025) against the standing feeder AMI dataset (ALN-214_AMI_Interval_Load_Export.xlsx) and applicable program standards as of 07/14/2025. The audit identified two material errors in the v1 memorandum:
[P16] (List Bullet): 1. Improper Use of Unrestricted Overnight Minimum Load in Violation of SRP-3 Rev 3 §4: Effective 02/10/2025, SRP-3 Rev 3 replaced the single unrestricted 24-hour minimum-load screen of SRP-3 Rev 2 with resource-specific evaluation windows under §4. For non-dispatchable solar photovoltaic resources without storage, SRP-3 Rev 3 §4 mandates that the 100%-of-minimum-load screen be evaluated exclusively over the daytime window of 10:00 to 16:00 local clock time, and explicitly provides that 'Overnight and early-morning minimum loads occur during hours of zero solar output and shall not be used to screen solar resources.' In IS-BRAM-2025-06-25 v1, the analyst applied the superseded unrestricted all-hours minimum load of 1.1 MW (1,100 kW), which occurred overnight on 03/23/2025 at 03:45 (Excel Row 25460) during zero solar generation. Within the mandatory 10:00–16:00 daytime window across the 12-month AMI record, the lowest feeder load recorded on Feeder ALN-214 is 2.4 MW (2,400 kW), occurring on 02/12/2025 at 11:30 (Excel Row 21747).
[P17] (List Bullet): 2. Inaccurate Citation of AMI Data Window and Interval Cadence Under SRP-3 Rev 3 §5: Memo IS-BRAM-2025-06-25 v1 reported a data window of '06/24/2024 – 06/24/2025' and an interval cadence of 'Sixty (60) minutes.' However, SRP-3 Rev 3 §5 requires use of the twelve (12) consecutive calendar months immediately preceding screening at a 15-minute interval cadence where available. The standing AMI export on file for Feeder ALN-214 (ALN-214_AMI_Interval_Load_Export.xlsx) covers the full 12 consecutive calendar months from 07/01/2024 00:00 through 06/30/2025 23:45 at a 15-minute interval cadence (35,040 consecutive 15-minute intervals, 100.0% data completeness).
[P19] (Normal): 3. Quantitative Analysis of Feeder ALN-214 AMI Interval Load Data (ALN-214_AMI_Interval_Load_Export.xlsx)
[P20] (Normal): Interconnection Studies performed a complete programmatic verification of the standing AMI interval load export for Feeder ALN-214 (/filesystem/Studies/ALN-214_AMI_Interval_Load_Export.xlsx, Sheet 'AMI Interval Load', Rows 5 to 35044) in accordance with SRP-3 Rev 3 §§4–5 and DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.2(a):
[P21] (List Bullet): Dataset Completeness and Data Hygiene (SRP-3 Rev 3 §5): The dataset contains 35,040 fifteen-minute interval readings spanning 365 days from 07/01/2024 00:00:00 (Row 5: 6,624 kW) through 06/30/2025 23:45:00 (Row 35044: 6,108 kW), achieving 100.0% interval completeness against the ≥95% requirement of SRP-3 Rev 3 §5. All 35,040 intervals contain positive valid load measurements between 1,100 kW and 8,526 kW. Zero intervals are missing, null, zero, negative, or flagged for forced/planned outages or abnormal feeder switching transfers.
[P22] (List Bullet): Annual Peak Feeder Load and Fast-Track 15%-of-Peak-Load Verification (DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.2(a)): The maximum interval load recorded on Feeder ALN-214 across the 12-month period is 8,526 kW (8.526 MW), occurring on 08/01/2024 at 13:30:00 (Row 3035). Under DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.2(a), the 15%-of-peak-load fast-track threshold is 0.15 × 8,526 kW = 1,278.9 kW (1.2789 MW, or ~1.28 MW). Bramwick Commons Solar's 1,800 kW (1.8 MW) capacity equals 21.11% of Feeder ALN-214's annual peak load (exceeding the 1,278.9 kW ceiling by 521.1 kW), confirming that the application properly failed Initial Fast-Track Screen 4.2(a) and was properly routed to Supplemental Review.
[P23] (List Bullet): Daytime Minimum Load Evaluation (10:00–16:00 Local Clock Time) Under SRP-3 Rev 3 §4: Per SRP-3 Rev 3 §4, the daytime window for solar photovoltaic resources is evaluated over intervals whose start time falls within 10:00–16:00 local clock time. Across all 365 days in ALN-214_AMI_Interval_Load_Export.xlsx, whether evaluated inclusive of the 16:00 interval start time (10:00 through 16:00 inclusive; 25 intervals/day = 9,125 intervals) or over the 6-hour block from 10:00 through 15:45 (24 intervals/day = 8,760 intervals), the absolute minimum daytime load on Feeder ALN-214 is identically 2,400 kW (2.4 MW / 2.40 MW), recorded on Wednesday, 02/12/2025 at 11:30:00 (Excel Row 21747).
[P24] (List Bullet): Sensitivity Verification Across 60-Minute Aggregations: Even if the 15-minute dataset were subsampled at top-of-hour (:00) 60-minute timestamps (8,760 hourly readings), the 10:00–16:00 daytime minimum load is 2,418 kW (2.418 MW on 01/25/2025 at 10:00, Row 20013; 1.8 MW / 2.418 MW = 74.44% ≤ 100%). If aggregated into 60-minute four-interval arithmetic averages, the 10:00–16:00 daytime minimum hourly load is 2,603.75 kW (2.604 MW on 01/26/2025 10:00–10:45; 1.8 MW / 2.60375 MW = 69.13% ≤ 100%). (Similarly, in the 8,760-hour Wiki summary extract, daytime 10:00–16:00 minimums are ~2.4 MW [2,401 kW at 14:00 on 07/14/2024]). Under every valid daytime formulation, the daytime minimum load is 2.4 MW (2,400 kW) and the 1.8 MW project passes with substantial margin.
[P26] (Normal): 4. Verification of DER Program Records as of Record Date 07/14/2025
[P27] (Normal): Per SRP-3 Rev 3 §4, the 100%-of-minimum-load screen compares the applicable feeder minimum load against the aggregate DER capacity on the feeder, defined as: (a) existing in-service DER capacity + (b) queued DER capacity ahead of the applicant + (c) the applicant's requested DER capacity. [P29] (Normal): 5. Screen-by-Screen Technical Determinations and Quantitative Basis
[P30] (Normal): 5.1 Summary of Initial Fast-Track Screening Determinations (DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.2 & Tariff §12.1)
[P31] (Normal): Before entering Supplemental Review, Bramwick Commons Solar (1.8 MW AC, Feeder ALN-214) was evaluated against the seven initial fast-track screens of DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.2. [P33] (Normal): 5.2 Supplemental Review Screen Determinations (SRP-3 Rev 3 §§3–5, DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.3 & Tariff §12.2)
[P34] (Normal): Under SRP-3 Rev 3 §3, Supplemental Review comprises three technical screens: (1) the Minimum-Load Screen (100% of applicable minimum load per §4), (2) the Voltage and Power-Quality Screen, and (3) the Safety and Reliability Screen. Per SRP-3 Rev 3 §3, because Bramwick Commons Solar was routed to Supplemental Review solely due to failure of the 15%-of-peak-load fast-track screen (DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.2(a)) and no voltage, thermal, or protection anomaly is flagged on Feeder ALN-214, the 100%-of-Minimum-Load Screen (§4) is the governing screen for Supplemental Review disposition. All three Supplemental Review screens have been evaluated and are determined as follows:

[P37] (Normal): Determination Call: 1.8 MW (1,800 kW) requested and aggregate DER capacity on Feeder ALN-214 is below the 2.4 MW (2,400 kW) daytime minimum feeder load (75.0% of daytime minimum load; +0.6 MW / +600 kW margin) — screen PASSED.

[P40] (Normal): While Bramwick Commons Solar passes Supplemental Review without triggering a System Impact Study, the Interconnection Service Agreement (ISA) drafted under Tariff §12.2 and DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.3 must incorporate the standard facility protection and telemetry requirements applicable to a 1.8 MW pure-export DER facility:

Classification: Technical Standard — Distributed Energy Resource Interconnection
Distribution: DER Program Office; Interconnection Studies; Distribution Planning; Standards Engineering;
Regulatory Affairs

§1 Purpose
This procedure defines the supplemental review process applied to distributed energy resource (DER)
interconnection applications that fail one or more of the fast-track technical screens set out in the Alleniom DER
Interconnection Standard (DIS-01 Rev 4). It establishes the ordered screens, data sources, and documentation to
be produced by the interconnection engineer conducting supplemental review, and identifies the conditions under
which a study agreement is required before the application may proceed.
Supplemental review is intended to allow an application that fails an initial fast-track screen to be evaluated
against a bounded set of additional technical criteria without incurring the cost and schedule of a full system
impact study, where that evaluation can be completed from existing feeder data and standard engineering
judgment.
Nothing in this procedure alters the substantive interconnection standards contained in DIS-01, the protection
requirements contained in DPS-07, or the telemetry and communications requirements contained in TCS-02.

§2 Scope
This procedure applies to:
(a) all in-scope DER interconnection applications (≥500 kW) as defined in DIS-01 §3 that have entered
supplemental review following failure of an initial screen; and
(b) all DER classes recognized in DIS-01 §3 — commercial small-scale (500 kW – 1 MW) and medium-scale (1
MW – 5 MW).
This procedure does not apply to:
(a) sub-500 kW installations processed under the Simplified Small-Systems Process;
(b) capacity or point-of-interconnection changes to an executed interconnection service agreement, which are
governed by DIS-01 §7; or
(c) domestic rooftop solar, which is out of scope for the DER Program.
Where a supplemental-review screen result is inconclusive on the record before the engineer, the application shall
be advanced to a study agreement rather than passed or failed under this procedure.

§3 Screens

SRP-3 Rev 3 — Supplemental Review Procedure · Effective 02/10/2025 · Alleniom Utilities — Standards Engineering

Page 1

 Applications entering supplemental review shall be evaluated under the following screens, in the order given. An
application that fails any screen shall be considered a candidate for a study agreement; the reviewing engineer
shall document the failing screen, the underlying data, and the recommended disposition per §6.
Screen A — Aggregate DER penetration on the feeder. Total nameplate DER (existing plus queued plus
requested) on the subject feeder shall not exceed the applicable penetration threshold set in DIS-01. Queue
positions are those on record with the DER Program Office at the date of screen evaluation.
Screen B — Voltage regulation and flicker. Reviewed against the feeder's most recent planning study or, where
none is on file for the subject feeder within twenty-four (24) months, against a screening voltage-rise calculation
performed using conductor and transformer impedance from the distribution planning record.
Screen C — Short-circuit contribution. DER short-circuit contribution shall not cause any feeder-protective
device to exceed 87.5% of its interrupting rating, nor cause any downstream protection coordination margin to
fall below the values specified in DPS-07.
Screen D — 100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar. Governed by §4.
Screen E — Reverse power flow at substation. Where the aggregate DER on the subject feeder exceeds the
substation transformer's certified reverse-power capability, or where reverse-power protective settings are not in
place, the application shall be routed to study.
Passing all applicable screens is a necessary but not sufficient condition for interconnection; the application
remains subject to the balance of the DIS-01 evaluation, including protection and telemetry requirements.

§4 100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar
100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar. For solar DER, the minimum load used in this screen shall be the
minimum load within the daytime window 10:00–16:00, determined from feeder AMI interval data. The absolute
overnight minimum shall NOT be used. Requested DER capacity must be ≤ this daytime-window minimum for
the site to pass the screen.
The daytime-window minimum shall be computed from feeder AMI interval data covering the most recent
complete twelve (12) calendar months, aggregated to fifteen-minute intervals aligned to the feeder AMI
collection cadence, and evaluated only over intervals whose start time falls within 10:00–16:00 local clock time
on the feeder. Intervals affected by known feeder outages, load transfers, or planned switching shall be excluded
and the exclusion documented in the reviewer's worksheet. Where fewer than twelve (12) months of AMI interval
data are available, the reviewer shall use the longest continuous complete period available and note the
data-window length in the supplemental review memo.
The daytime-window minimum determined under this section is the sole minimum-load figure used for the solar
100%-of-minimum-load screen. Feeder minimum-load figures produced for other purposes — planning studies,
hosting-capacity map inputs, protection coordination — are not substitutes for the value computed under this
section and shall not be carried into the Screen D determination without recomputation on the AMI record.
Where a prior supplemental review memo on the same feeder has applied a different minimum-load basis, the
reviewer shall recompute the value under this section and, if the two disagree, supersede the earlier memo in the
file.

§5 Data sources
The following data sources are authoritative for supplemental review under this procedure:

SRP-3 Rev 3 — Supplemental Review Procedure · Effective 02/10/2025 · Alleniom Utilities — Standards Engineering

Page 2

 (a) Feeder AMI interval data — from the Alleniom AMI Data Warehouse, at the meter aggregation level
published for the subject feeder. AMI interval data is the sole authoritative source for the Screen D
minimum-load determination described in §4.
(b) Distribution planning record — most recent feeder planning study, conductor and transformer impedance
data, and protection coordination settings, held by Distribution Planning.
(c) DER queue — active-queue and on-hold registers maintained by the DER Program Office as of the screen
evaluation date. Queue entries not yet reflected in a published hosting-capacity map remain applicable to Screen
A.
(d) Certified Equipment List (CEL) — current edition, for verification that proposed inverters and PCS
equipment are eligible to be considered under the screens.
(e) Interconnection application record — the applicant's filed capacity, single-line diagram, inverter
specifications, and control narrative (where controlled-capacity operation is asserted under DIS-01 §3.6).
Substitution of a source not listed above shall be documented in the memo produced under §6, together with the
reason for the substitution.

§6 Documentation
The reviewing engineer shall produce a supplemental review memo for each application processed under this
procedure. The memo shall contain, at minimum:
(a) application identifier, applicant, subject feeder, and requested capacity;
(b) the screens applied and the pass/fail determination for each;
(c) for Screen D, the daytime-window minimum load determined per §4, the data window used, the count of
intervals evaluated, and any interval exclusions with reason;
(d) the recommended disposition — advance without study agreement, advance to study agreement, or return to
applicant with specified deficiency;
(e) reviewer signature and date; and
(f) the identifiers of any earlier supplemental review memos superseded.
The memo shall be filed to the interconnection application record within five (5) business days of screen
completion. Where a memo supersedes an earlier determination on the same application or the same feeder, the
superseded memo shall be flagged in the file and a cross-reference to the superseding memo added to its cover.

The program-scope threshold is 500 kW. Facilities below 500 kW, whether commercial or residential in customer
class, are routed to the Simplified Small-Systems Process and are not administered by the DER Program.

§3.1 Determination of aggregate nameplate capacity
Aggregate nameplate capacity is the sum of the manufacturer-rated ac output ratings of all generating equipment
interconnected, or proposed to be interconnected, at a single point of common coupling. Manufacturer datasheets
govern; derated or "operating" figures do not substitute for nameplate except as provided in §3.6.

§3.2 Point of common coupling
The point of common coupling is the point at which the DER facility is electrically connected to the Company's
distribution system, as further defined in IEEE 1547-2018. The PCC is distinct from the point of interconnection (POI),
the latter being the physical demarcation of Company-owned protective and metering equipment.

§3.3 Determination on the basis of application
Classification is determined on the facility as filed and as physically configured on site. Filing captions, project titles,
and cover-letter characterizations do not alter classification; the connection diagram, the equipment schedule, and
the address of record govern.

§3.4 Aggregation
Co-located DER behind the same point of common coupling counts toward one site total.
Previously interconnected legacy equipment counts toward the aggregate regardless of the vintage of its permission
to operate, regardless of whether it predates any current Alleniom standard, and regardless of the sequence or form
in which subsequent applications are submitted at the same PCC. The aggregate governs the facility class and the
resulting program-scope determination.
An applicant proposing a new DER at a premises that already hosts DER shall identify the existing equipment on the
application form and shall submit a one-line diagram showing the electrical relationship of the proposed equipment,
the existing equipment, the customer load, the customer meter, and the PCC. Interconnection Studies verifies against
the Company existing-DER register.

§3.5 Shared-POI eligibility
A new DER may share an existing POI only where the combined facility, including legacy equipment, can be brought
to current monitoring/control standards; otherwise a separate POI and a new application are required. Where the
existing system operates behind the meter, a new DER may instead be interconnected front-of-the-meter under its
own service and POI, and is then evaluated on its own capacity without aggregation.

DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard

Page 3

 DIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024

The two dispositions available under §3.5 are:
1. Shared POI, aggregated. The combined facility (legacy equipment plus proposed equipment) is brought to
current monitoring/control standards as prescribed by TCS-02 and by Table 5-1 at the aggregate class. The
applicant is responsible for the retrofit and for demonstrating retrofit feasibility to Interconnection Studies. Where
feasibility is confirmed, the application proceeds at the aggregate capacity at the shared POI.
2. Separate POI, non-aggregated front-of-the-meter alternative. Where the existing system operates behind
the meter and the applicant elects to interconnect the new DER front-of-the-meter under a separate service and
its own POI, the new DER is evaluated on its own capacity, without aggregation with the legacy equipment.
Class placement, review path, and Table 5-1 category are determined from the new DER's capacity alone.
Retrofit feasibility of legacy equipment is a factual question the Company will not decide from records alone; the
applicant or its authorized developer must confirm feasibility in writing. Absent that confirmation, the shared-POI path
under §3.5(1) is not available and the application is redirected to §3.5(2) or withdrawn.

§3.6 Controlled-capacity recognition
A limit below nameplate is recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification plus an approved Control
Narrative — sufficient in themselves for recognition. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
recognized limit is enforced as applicable: telemetry monitoring, and on pure-generation sites the POI recloser's ANSI
32 directional-power element set to the recognized limit and tripping on violation.
Required submissions. To have a controlled operating limit recognized in place of aggregate nameplate for
program-scope and study purposes, the applicant shall submit both of the following:
1. A valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where
applicable) and/or UL 3141, identifying the specific equipment arrangement at the applicant's site and the
setpoint range.
2. An approved Control Narrative — a written engineering document describing how the site's control system
enforces the requested operating limit, including the sensed quantities, the response actions, the response
times, the interlocks, and any allowable modes and their setpoint ceilings.
These two documents, taken together, are sufficient in themselves to establish recognition of the controlled limit.
Recognition establishes the capacity at which the facility is reviewed, classified, and studied.
Enforcement backstops as arrangement provides. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
recognized limit is enforced by the arrangement's existing equipment as follows:
• Telemetry monitoring. For sites at or above the TCS-02 threshold, the Company's RTU-to-SCADA telemetry
monitors real-power export at the point of interconnection against the recognized limit. Sustained deviation
triggers investigation under TCS-02 and may result in a hold on permission to operate.

    32	against a bounded set of additional technical criteria without incurring the cost and schedule of a full system
    33	impact study, where that evaluation can be completed from existing feeder data and standard engineering

    95	§1 Purpose and Scope
    96	This standard establishes the technical and procedural requirements for interconnection of distributed energy

   220	§3.1 Determination of aggregate nameplate capacity
   221	Aggregate nameplate capacity is the sum of the manufacturer-rated ac output ratings of all generating equipment
   222	interconnected, or proposed to be interconnected, at a single point of common coupling. Manufacturer datasheets
   223	govern; derated or "operating" figures do not substitute for nameplate except as provided in §3.6.
   224	
   225	§3.2 Point of common coupling
   226	The point of common coupling is the point at which the DER facility is electrically connected to the Company's
   227	distribution system, as further defined in IEEE 1547-2018. The PCC is distinct from the point of interconnection (POI),
   228	the latter being the physical demarcation of Company-owned protective and metering equipment.
   229	
   230	§3.3 Determination on the basis of application
   231	Classification is determined on the facility as filed and as physically configured on site. Filing captions, project titles,
   232	and cover-letter characterizations do not alter classification; the connection diagram, the equipment schedule, and
   233	the address of record govern.
   234	
   235	§3.4 Aggregation
   236	Co-located DER behind the same point of common coupling counts toward one site total.
   237	Previously interconnected legacy equipment counts toward the aggregate regardless of the vintage of its permission
   238	to operate, regardless of whether it predates any current Alleniom standard, and regardless of the sequence or form
   239	in which subsequent applications are submitted at the same PCC. The aggregate governs the facility class and the
   240	resulting program-scope determination.
   241	An applicant proposing a new DER at a premises that already hosts DER shall identify the existing equipment on the
   242	application form and shall submit a one-line diagram showing the electrical relationship of the proposed equipment,
   243	the existing equipment, the customer load, the customer meter, and the PCC. Interconnection Studies verifies against
   244	the Company existing-DER register.
   245	
   246	§3.5 Shared-POI eligibility
   247	A new DER may share an existing POI only where the combined facility, including legacy equipment, can be brought
   248	to current monitoring/control standards; otherwise a separate POI and a new application are required. Where the
   249	existing system operates behind the meter, a new DER may instead be interconnected front-of-the-meter under its
   250	own service and POI, and is then evaluated on its own capacity without aggregation.
   251	
   252	DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard
   253	
   254	Page 3
   255	
   256	 DIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024
   257	
   258	The two dispositions available under §3.5 are:
   259	1. Shared POI, aggregated. The combined facility (legacy equipment plus proposed equipment) is brought to
   260	current monitoring/control standards as prescribed by TCS-02 and by Table 5-1 at the aggregate class. The
   261	applicant is responsible for the retrofit and for demonstrating retrofit feasibility to Interconnection Studies. Where
   262	feasibility is confirmed, the application proceeds at the aggregate capacity at the shared POI.
   263	2. Separate POI, non-aggregated front-of-the-meter alternative. Where the existing system operates behind
   264	the meter and the applicant elects to interconnect the new DER front-of-the-meter under a separate service and
   265	its own POI, the new DER is evaluated on its own capacity, without aggregation with the legacy equipment.
   266	Class placement, review path, and Table 5-1 category are determined from the new DER's capacity alone.
   267	Retrofit feasibility of legacy equipment is a factual question the Company will not decide from records alone; the
   268	applicant or its authorized developer must confirm feasibility in writing. Absent that confirmation, the shared-POI path
   269	under §3.5(1) is not available and the application is redirected to §3.5(2) or withdrawn.
   270	
   271	§3.6 Controlled-capacity recognition
   272	A limit below nameplate is recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification plus an approved Control
   273	Narrative — sufficient in themselves for recognition. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
   274	recognized limit is enforced as applicable: telemetry monitoring, and on pure-generation sites the POI recloser's ANSI
   275	32 directional-power element set to the recognized limit and tripping on violation.
   276	Required submissions. To have a controlled operating limit recognized in place of aggregate nameplate for
   277	program-scope and study purposes, the applicant shall submit both of the following:
   278	1. A valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where
   279	applicable) and/or UL 3141, identifying the specific equipment arrangement at the applicant's site and the
   280	setpoint range.
   281	2. An approved Control Narrative — a written engineering document describing how the site's control system
   282	enforces the requested operating limit, including the sensed quantities, the response actions, the response
   283	times, the interlocks, and any allowable modes and their setpoint ceilings.
   284	These two documents, taken together, are sufficient in themselves to establish recognition of the controlled limit.
   285	Recognition establishes the capacity at which the facility is reviewed, classified, and studied.
   286	Enforcement backstops as arrangement provides. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
   287	recognized limit is enforced by the arrangement's existing equipment as follows:
   288	• Telemetry monitoring. For sites at or above the TCS-02 threshold, the Company's RTU-to-SCADA telemetry
   289	monitors real-power export at the point of interconnection against the recognized limit. Sustained deviation
   290	triggers investigation under TCS-02 and may result in a hold on permission to operate.
   291	• POI recloser directional-power element (pure-generation sites). On pure-generation sites — sites at which
   292	no customer load is served behind the point of common coupling — where a utility POI recloser is installed per
   293	Table 5-1 and DPS-07, the recloser's ANSI 32 directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips
   294	the site on violation. The ANSI 32 element is inherently available in modern reclosers and does not require
   295	additional utility hardware.
   296	Enforcement provisions apply only as the site's arrangement provides them. Their absence at a particular site does
   297	not reopen the recognition determination once the two required submissions are on file.
   298	No controlled limit without submissions. In the absence of both a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification and
   299	an approved Control Narrative, nameplate governs for classification, program-scope determination, and study.
   300	Certified Equipment List. CEL-2025-Q2 restates this section in its front matter. Listing of a PCS on the current CEL
   301	does not by itself constitute recognition of a controlled limit for a particular site; the applicant's site-specific

[P11]: 1. Project Identification and Subject Feeder Baseline (As of 07/14/2025)
[P12]: Bramwick Commons Solar LLC submitted an interconnection application for the Bramwick Commons Solar project, a 1.8 MW AC (1,800 kW) pure-export front-of-the-meter solar photovoltaic generating facility proposing to interconnect to Feeder ALN-214 out of Larkspur Ridge Substation (12.47 kV nominal primary voltage). Because the facility's nameplate capacity is ≥ 500 kW and ≤ 2.0 MW, the application falls within the commercial DER Program scope under DIS-01 Rev 4 §3.1 and within the Fast-Track eligibility ceiling under DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.1 and Tariff §12.1. Following failure of the initial fast-track 15%-of-peak-load screen (DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.2(a)), the application was routed to Supplemental Review pursuant to DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.3, Tariff §12.2, and SRP-3 Rev 3 §2.

IS-BRAM-2025-06-25, Rev v1, signed by Priya Ranganathan and countersigned by Meera Vellanki on 06/25/2025) against the standing feeder AMI dataset (ALN-214_AMI_Interval_Load_Export.xlsx) and applicable program standards as of 07/14/2025. The audit identified two material errors in the v1 memorandum:
[P16]: 1. Improper Use of Unrestricted Overnight Minimum Load in Violation of SRP-3 Rev 3 §4: Effective 02/10/2025, SRP-3 Rev 3 replaced the single unrestricted 24-hour minimum-load screen of SRP-3 Rev 2 with resource-specific evaluation windows under §4. For non-dispatchable solar photovoltaic resources without storage, SRP-3 Rev 3 §4 mandates that the 100%-of-minimum-load screen be evaluated exclusively over the daytime window of 10:00 to 16:00 local clock time, and explicitly provides that 'Overnight and early-morning minimum loads occur during hours of zero solar output and shall not be used to screen solar resources.' In IS-BRAM-2025-06-25 v1, the analyst applied the superseded unrestricted all-hours minimum load of 1.1 MW (1,100 kW), which occurred overnight on 03/23/2025 at 03:45 (Excel Row 25460) during zero solar generation. Within the mandatory 10:00–16:00 daytime window across the 12-month AMI record, the lowest feeder load recorded on Feeder ALN-214 is 2.4 MW (2,400 kW), occurring on 02/12/2025 at 11:30 (Excel Row 21747).
[P17]: 2. Inaccurate Citation of AMI Data Window and Interval Cadence Under SRP-3 Rev 3 §5: Memo IS-BRAM-2025-06-25 v1 reported a data window of '06/24/2024 – 06/24/2025' and an interval cadence of 'Sixty (60) minutes.' However, SRP-3 Rev 3 §5 requires use of the twelve (12) consecutive calendar months immediately preceding screening at a 15-minute interval cadence where available. The standing AMI export on file for Feeder ALN-214 (ALN-214_AMI_Interval_Load_Export.xlsx) covers the full 12 consecutive calendar months from 07/01/2024 00:00 through 06/30/2025 23:45 at a 15-minute interval cadence (35,040 consecutive 15-minute intervals, 100.0% data completeness).

[P21]: Dataset Completeness and Data Hygiene (SRP-3 Rev 3 §5): The dataset contains 35,040 fifteen-minute interval readings spanning 365 days from 07/01/2024 00:00:00 (Row 5: 6,624 kW) through 06/30/2025 23:45:00 (Row 35044: 6,108 kW), achieving 100.0% interval completeness against the ≥95% requirement of SRP-3 Rev 3 §5. All 35,040 intervals contain positive valid load measurements between 1,100 kW and 8,526 kW. Zero intervals are missing, null, zero, negative, or flagged for forced/planned outages or abnormal feeder switching transfers.
[P22]: Annual Peak Feeder Load and Fast-Track 15%-of-Peak-Load Verification (DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.2(a)): The maximum interval load recorded on Feeder ALN-214 across the 12-month period is 8,526 kW (8.526 MW), occurring on 08/01/2024 at 13:30:00 (Row 3035). Under DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.2(a), the 15%-of-peak-load fast-track threshold is 0.15 × 8,526 kW = 1,278.9 kW (1.2789 MW, or ~1.28 MW). Bramwick Commons Solar's 1,800 kW (1.8 MW) capacity equals 21.11% of Feeder ALN-214's annual peak load (exceeding the 1,278.9 kW ceiling by 521.1 kW), confirming that the application properly failed Initial Fast-Track Screen 4.2(a) and was properly routed to Supplemental Review.

[P29]: 5. Screen-by-Screen Technical Determinations and Quantitative Basis
[P30]: 5.1 Summary of Initial Fast-Track Screening Determinations (DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.2 & Tariff §12.1)
[P31]: Before entering Supplemental Review, Bramwick Commons Solar (1.8 MW AC, Feeder ALN-214) was evaluated against the seven initial fast-track screens of DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.2. [P33]: 5.2 Supplemental Review Screen Determinations (SRP-3 Rev 3 §§3–5, DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.3 & Tariff §12.2)
[P34]: Under SRP-3 Rev 3 §3, Supplemental Review comprises three technical screens: (1) the Minimum-Load Screen (100% of applicable minimum load per §4), (2) the Voltage and Power-Quality Screen, and (3) the Safety and Reliability Screen. [P37]: Determination Call: 1.8 MW (1,800 kW) requested and aggregate DER capacity on Feeder ALN-214 is below the 2.4 MW (2,400 kW) daytime minimum feeder load (75.0% of daytime minimum load; +0.6 MW / +600 kW margin) — screen PASSED.
[P39]: 7. Applicable Protection, Telemetry, and Equipment Requirements for ISA Scope
[P40]: While Bramwick Commons Solar passes Supplemental Review without triggering a System Impact Study, the Interconnection Service Agreement (ISA) drafted under Tariff §12.2 and DIS-01 Rev 4 §4.3 must incorporate the standard facility protection and telemetry requirements applicable to a 1.8 MW pure-export DER facility:
[P41]: Utility-Owned POI Recloser Required (DIS-01 Rev 4 §5.2, DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2, and ERP-9 Rev 2 §3): Because Bramwick Commons Solar has an aggregate AC nameplate capacity of 1.8 MW (> 1.0 MW threshold) and is a pure-export generation facility with no significant co-located load, both DIS-01 Rev 4 §5.2 and DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2 unconditionally require a utility-owned, SCADA-controlled distribution-class POI recloser (implementing ANSI functions 50/51, 50N/51N, 27/59, 81U/81O, 25, 32, and 79 with visible-break lockable disconnect per DPS-07 §4.2). DER Program Office —

Attached please find the City of Elmsworth's DER interconnection application for the Municipal Service Center PV project (Form DIS-APP-01), assigned Application ID PXA-2025-0198 on your intake page. Nameplate is 900 kW AC, behind-the-meter with export capability, mounted on the Municipal Service Center rooftop and adjacent parking canopy.

For your records, this filing follows our earlier application PXA-2023-0412 dated 04/12/2023 for the same Municipal Service Center site. The 2023 filing sat with our office through a budget cycle change and a facilities director turnover on our side, and we did not push it forward during that period. The scope in the current package is materially the same site, the same 900 kW envelope, and the same point of interconnection area on the mid-town Elmsworth feeder — the update is the CEL-2025-Q2 inverter selection and refreshed drawings dated 05/16/2025.

Given the continuity of the project, we would like to retain our original 2023 queue position. Council approved the capital allocation in the FY25 budget on the assumption that we would be in construction this fall, and every month we slide back in the queue is a month that pushes mechanical completion past the winter shutdown window and into next spring. We would appreciate your team's confirmation on that point at your earliest convenience so we can lock in permit and procurement dates.

We are targeting the following applicant-side milestones (also carried in Section 7 of the application):

  - Permit set complete: 08/2025
  - Construction start: 10/2025
  - Mechanical completion: 02/2026
  - Ready for witness test: 03/2026

From: Rosa Camarena <rosa.camarena@brookfenusd.org>
To: der.program@alleniom.com
Cc: Dana Whitcomb <dana.whitcomb@alleniom.com>, Harriet Ngoyi <harriet.ngoyi@alleniom.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:42:18 -0500
Subject: Urgent: school array energization priority
Message-ID: <20250630-094218-rc-brookfen@brookfenusd.org>
X-Mailer: Brookfen USD Mail
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 7bit

To the DER Program Office:

I am writing again — and I want to be direct about the fact that this is not the first, second, or third time I have raised this with your office — to ask for a firm answer on when Alleniom Utilities intends to energize the two solar arrays serving Brookfen Unified School District. This message is dated 06/30/2025 and I would like a written response before the end of next week.

The two arrays in question, and their status on our side, are as follows:

  • Brookfen North High School Array — 720 kW. Construction was declared complete by our contractor on 04/18/2025. The local electrical inspector closed out the installation the same week. The system has been standing idle, energized-ready, for more than ten weeks.

  • Brookfen West Elementary Array — 640 kW. Construction was declared complete on 05/23/2025. Inspection was closed out shortly thereafter. This system has now been standing idle for over a month.

Neither array has been energized. Neither array has a firm energization date on record with the District. Each time our office contacts your program inbox we are told that a component — variously described as a "telemetry unit" or an "RTU" — has not yet been delivered by your supplier, and that we are somewhere in a queue behind other sites. What we have never been given, in writing, is the position of our sites in that queue, the identity of the sites ahead of us, or the basis on which those sites are being served ahead of ours.

I have to tell you plainly that the patience of the Brookfen school board and the District's superintendent is exhausted. The 2025–2026 school year begins for our students on 08/26/2025. Both of these arrays were financed, in significant part, on the strength of first-year operating-cost savings that were built into the District's adopted budget for that same school year and presented to our board and to the community at public meetings. Every additional week that these systems sit dark is a week of budgeted savings the District will not realize and will have to explain to the board, to our parents, and to the taxpayers of Brookfen who approved the underlying bond measure. Our high school's building-systems curriculum was also structured around students being able to observe the array in operation from the beginning of the term; that piece of the school year is now at risk of slipping into the second semester or being cut altogether.

You will by now have received the Alleron Municipal League's letter of 06/20/2025, signed by Executive Director Alden Pryce, escalating this same set of concerns on behalf of the District and thirteen other League members. Brookfen USD is one of the members named in that letter and stands fully behind the requests it contains. This message is not a substitute for the League's letter; it is intended to make the District's individual position, and the specifics of our two sites, unmistakable to your office.

What I am asking for, directly, is this: in the next allocation of the equipment your program office is holding up as the constraint — the RTU / telemetry units your staff have referenced in prior calls — I am asking Alleniom Utilities to advance the District's two waiting arrays ahead of the other sites presently competing for those units. Brookfen North completed construction on 04/18/2025 and Brookfen West on 05/23/2025. Both are public school facilities. Both have children returning to the building in eight weeks. Neither array can wait for a second or third delivery cycle without meaningful harm to the District's fiscal position and to the educational program these systems were installed to support.

If there is a formal process for requesting that our two sites be advanced in your next equipment allocation, please tell me what that process is and I will follow it today. If there is not, please treat this message as our written request under whatever mechanism your program uses to weigh these decisions, and please confirm receipt.

I am copying Ms. Whitcomb and Ms. Ngoyi so that this request is on the record with senior distribution operations and regulatory affairs, and so that no one at your program office is later in a position to say the District did not put this in writing in time.

I would like a written reply — not a call-back, a written reply — by close of business Friday, 07/11/2025. Silence past that date will require the District to raise this matter again through the League and, if necessary, directly with the Commission's Energy Resources Division, whose staff we understand is already tracking this program.

I am available at (612) 448-0311 during District business hours if it would help to talk any of this through. I would strongly prefer to resolve it with your office.

Regards,

Rosa Camarena
Facilities Director
Brookfen Unified School District
1725 Grantway Drive, Brookfen, Alleron 12BR
(612) 448-0311

   Alleniom Utilities — Regulatory Affairs
   4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
   INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
   TO: DER Program Manager
   CC: Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations
   Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies
   Ivo Grantham, Manager, DER Planning Group
   FROM: Harriet Ngoyi, Director, Regulatory Affairs
   DATE: 07/01/2025
   SUBJECT: DER Backlog Review — Program Manager Tasking
   1. Confirmation of directive
   This memorandum confirms and operationalizes the internal directive issued 06/27/2025 by Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations (DIR-2025-0627), ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. Regulatory Affairs accepts ownership of the external commitments arising from that directive and, by this memorandum, assigns the internal queue-cleanup work to the DER Program Manager.
   The scope of the backlog review, as established by the VP, is the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population of the commercial DER program queue as of the anchor date. Every application is to be accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action. Nothing in this memorandum reduces, expands, or alters that scope.
   2. Governing deadlines
   Two dates fix the outer boundary of this work and are not to be revisited without written concurrence from the VP office and Regulatory Affairs:
   08/15/2025 — Response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs will issue the formal written response to the League's 06/20/2025 letter. The response will be substantive and project-specific, addressing the League's five enumerated requests on behalf of the fourteen member municipalities and school districts. Regulatory Affairs is the signatory; the DER Program Manager is responsible for delivering the underlying queue accounting on which the response will rest.
   09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. The queue accounting must be complete and defensible in advance of the briefing to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission's Energy Resources Division. Regulatory Affairs will not present partial data to the Commission. Any application whose disposition remains open on 09/10/2025 must have a written reason on file, not an oral one.
   Any interim regulatory information request the Division may issue in advance of the briefing will be answered from the same underlying record and will not create a separate work product for the Program Manager beyond timely disposition of the affected applications.
   3. Tasking of the DER Program Manager
   The DER Program Manager is tasked, effective immediately, with producing the following queue-cleanup inputs. Each input is to be closed on the record — with the supporting document, tariff citation, standard, or operating guideline named in the file — before it is reported as complete.
   3.1 On-hold list dispositions. Work the current on-hold population by hold-reason category. For each project, determine the correct disposition under the applicable tariff provisions and program policy, and clear holds where the underlying reason has resolved. Cross-reference hold-reason categories against the relevant queue and financial records. Business-day counts must follow the standard business-day convention.
   3.2 Applications-intake corrections. Review the active queue for duplicate, ghost, and stale-status records. Where a customer has filed a new application at a site with a prior, silently abandoned filing, resolve the intake question in writing before either record is closed or merged. Queue-date assignment must follow the written policy.
   3.3 Standards-conflict routing. For every project currently sitting on a standards-clarification hold, determine and execute the correct disposition under applicable program standards and operating procedures.
   3.4 Equipment allocation. Convene the equipment-allocation determination for the sites that have completed construction and are awaiting utility-owned equipment. Rank the sites under the applicable equipment deployment prioritization guideline in accordance with its procedures, and match against the current supplier delivery schedule reported by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
   3.5 Aggregation determinations. For applications proposing new DER at sites that may host existing generation, apply the applicable aggregation provision before finalizing program-scope routing.
   3.6 Capacity verifications. For any application on abnormality hold due to a stated-vs-nameplate capacity discrepancy, verify the nameplate from the application's technical documentation and apply the applicable interconnection standard to any claimed operating limit below inverter nameplate.
   3.7 Hosting-capacity corrections. Before any capacity figure from the published hosting-capacity map is communicated externally, confirm that the figure reflects the current state of the affected feeder. A priority refresh is to be requested from Distribution Planning under the published refresh-prioritization criteria.
   3.8 Witness-test dispositions. Verify each inverter model against the applicable certified equipment list under the commissioning procedure in effect at the time of determination. Waiver eligibility is to be determined against the applicable certified equipment list.
   3.9 Supplemental-review reversals. Review any supplemental-review determination on file for consistency with current program procedures. Where the record requires revision, update the file and flag any prior memorandum that has been superseded accordingly.
   4. Reporting cadence
   The DER Program Manager will provide weekly progress reports to Regulatory Affairs, with copy to the VP office, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025 and continuing through 09/12/2025. The weekly report will comprise:
   counts by disposition category, aligned to the categories in §3 above;
   items closed on the record during the reporting week, with the governing citation named;
   exceptions requiring Regulatory Affairs or VP attention, including any project at risk of missing 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025;
   forward-look for the following reporting week.
   Reports are to be delivered in writing. Verbal updates do not substitute.
   5. General provisions
   Every disposition reached under this tasking must be tariff-defensible on the face of the file. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, operating guideline, or bulletin that supports the action. Where the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready and is to be held rather than reported.
   Follow the noticing, payment-deadline, and hold-clearance procedures as written. Standards or procedural conflicts route through the established referral process; they are not to be resolved informally in the queue. Queue-date treatment must remain within what the tariff and program policy permit.

   Feeder ALN-108 Planning Study — Post-Publication Update Q3 2024
   Alleniom Utilities — Distribution Planning
   DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
   Doc no. PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 · Rev 1 · Date 10/15/2024 · Owner: Distribution Planning
   Prepared by: June Halloway, Distribution Planning Engineer
   Contact: june.halloway@alleniom.com
   1. Purpose
   This memorandum constitutes an interim update to the published Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map (HCM-2024-Q2, published 05/15/2024) with respect to Feeder ALN-108 (Elderpine substation, 13.2 kV, pure-generation category). It is issued between scheduled quarterly refreshes of the Hosting Capacity Map to record a material queue addition on the subject feeder that has occurred since the last published map release, so that Distribution Planning staff, applicant-facing correspondence, and pre-application dialogue may be informed of a working interim figure until the next full refresh cycle.
   The scope of this document is limited to Feeder ALN-108. It does not modify the published values shown on any other feeder in HCM-2024-Q2, nor does it substitute for a formal feeder-level planning study in support of any specific interconnection application. Applicants and pre-application requesters seeking definitive feeder guidance for project scoping decisions should continue to consult Distribution Planning directly, and any project of consequential size on Feeder ALN-108 will require a full feeder-level planning study following the standard Alleniom Distribution Planning methodology.
   2. Baseline: Published Available Capacity
   The Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map was published on 05/15/2024. The map reflects, on a per-feeder basis, the published available capacity value derived from the most recent completed planning study of record for each feeder as of the publication date, incorporating recorded peak and minimum load, existing interconnected DER of record at the time of the underlying study, and standard thermal, voltage, and protection screens.
   For Feeder ALN-108, the published values on HCM-2024-Q2 are as follows:
   The 3.0 MW figure shown above is the baseline against which subsequent queue activity is netted for the purposes of this interim update. It remains, until the next scheduled quarterly refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map or an intervening full feeder re-study, the sole published available capacity of record for Feeder ALN-108.
   3. Post-Publication Queue Activity
   Distribution Planning has reviewed the Active Queue Report as of the date of this document to identify interconnection applications assigned to Feeder ALN-108 that have been queued subsequent to publication of the Hosting Capacity Map. The following post-publication queue entry has been identified on Feeder ALN-108:
   The 1.2 MW project queued on 09/18/2024 is a pure-generation interconnection request, consistent with the DER category assigned to the feeder in HCM-2024-Q2. It represents the sole queue addition on Feeder ALN-108 identified in the Active Queue Report between the publication date of the map (05/15/2024) and the date of this study.
   No other pending applications, executed interconnection service agreements, or in-service DER additions on Feeder ALN-108 have been identified since publication of HCM-2024-Q2 that would materially alter the baseline figure or the interim netted position stated below.
   4. Interim Netted Figure
   Applying the post-publication queue entry identified in Section 3 against the published available capacity of record stated in Section 2, the interim netted available capacity figure for Feeder ALN-108 as of the date of this document is calculated as follows:
   Interim available capacity: 3.0 MW − 1.2 MW = 1.8 MW.
   This interim figure is provided as a working reference for Distribution Planning staff and for use in pre-application correspondence concerning Feeder ALN-108 where such correspondence is issued between quarterly refreshes of the Hosting Capacity Map. The figure is not a substitute for, and does not supersede, the published available capacity value of record on HCM-2024-Q2; the published value remains 3.0 MW until the next map republication.
   The interim figure carries the following stated limitations:
   It reflects the state of the queue as of the date of this document only. Any subsequent queue additions, withdrawals, or reassignments affecting Feeder ALN-108 that post-date this study are not reflected in the figure above and will require Distribution Planning to reassess the interim position accordingly.
   It applies a straight-line nameplate netting against the published available capacity. A full feeder re-study, when performed, may yield a different available capacity value on Feeder ALN-108 depending on updated load recordings, revised existing-DER accounting, and the outcome of thermal, voltage, and protection screens as re-run against current data.
   The 1.2 MW queue entry is at the application/queue stage. Should that application be withdrawn or should its final capacity change following study or agreement negotiation, the interim netted figure would require corresponding adjustment.
   5. Recommendation
   Distribution Planning recommends the following:
   Distribution Planning staff should treat 1.8 MW as the working interim available capacity for Feeder ALN-108 in any pre-application dialogue, applicant correspondence, or internal scoping analysis conducted between the date of this document and the next scheduled refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map. The published 3.0 MW figure on HCM-2024-Q2 remains the value of record for the map itself and should not be altered on the published map absent republication.
   A refreshed feeder-level planning study for Feeder ALN-108 should be scheduled to be undertaken in advance of, and its results incorporated into, the next full quarterly refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map. Feeder ALN-108 should be included among the feeders prioritized for re-study on the criteria stated in the map front matter: application date of pending queue entries, capacity requested relative to published available headroom, and DER category (pure generation is weighted more heavily against feeder headroom than net-metering behind-the-meter interconnections at equivalent nameplate).
   This document should be reissued or superseded if any further queue activity on Feeder ALN-108 arises before the next quarterly map refresh, so that the working interim figure remains accurate as of its date of issue. Distribution Planning will monitor the Active Queue Report accordingly.
   Applicants inquiring about Feeder ALN-108 between the date of this document and the next scheduled map republication should be directed to Distribution Planning for confirmation of the interim position before finalizing project sizing decisions, consistent with the general applicability note carried in the front matter of HCM-2024-Q2.

SUBJECT: DER Backlog Review — Program Manager Tasking
1. Confirmation of directive
This memorandum confirms and operationalizes the internal directive issued 06/27/2025 by Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations (DIR-2025-0627), ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. Regulatory Affairs accepts ownership of the external commitments arising from that directive and, by this memorandum, assigns the internal queue-cleanup work to the DER Program Manager.
The scope of the backlog review, as established by the VP, is the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population of the commercial DER program queue as of the anchor date. Every application is to be accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action. Nothing in this memorandum reduces, expands, or alters that scope.
2. Governing deadlines
Two dates fix the outer boundary of this work and are not to be revisited without written concurrence from the VP office and Regulatory Affairs:
08/15/2025 — Response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs will issue the formal written response to the League's 06/20/2025 letter. The response will be substantive and project-specific, addressing the League's five enumerated requests on behalf of the fourteen member municipalities and school districts. Regulatory Affairs is the signatory; the DER Program Manager is responsible for delivering the underlying queue accounting on which the response will rest.
09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. The queue accounting must be complete and defensible in advance of the briefing to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission's Energy Resources Division. Regulatory Affairs will not present partial data to the Commission. Any application whose disposition remains open on 09/10/2025 must have a written reason on file, not an oral one.
Any interim regulatory information request the Division may issue in advance of the briefing will be answered from the same underlying record and will not create a separate work product for the Program Manager beyond timely disposition of the affected applications.
3. Tasking of the DER Program Manager
The DER Program Manager is tasked, effective immediately, with producing the following queue-cleanup inputs. Each input is to be closed on the record — with the supporting document, tariff citation, standard, or operating guideline named in the file — before it is reported as complete.
3.1 On-hold list dispositions. Work the current on-hold population by hold-reason category. For each project, determine the correct disposition under the applicable tariff provisions and program policy, and clear holds where the underlying reason has resolved. Cross-reference hold-reason categories against the relevant queue and financial records. Business-day counts must follow the standard business-day convention.
3.2 Applications-intake corrections. Review the active queue for duplicate, ghost, and stale-status records. Where a customer has filed a new application at a site with a prior, silently abandoned filing, resolve the intake question in writing before either record is closed or merged. Queue-date assignment must follow the written policy.
3.3 Standards-conflict routing. For every project currently sitting on a standards-clarification hold, determine and execute the correct disposition under applicable program standards and operating procedures.
3.4 Equipment allocation. Convene the equipment-allocation determination for the sites that have completed construction and are awaiting utility-owned equipment. Rank the sites under the applicable equipment deployment prioritization guideline in accordance with its procedures, and match against the current supplier delivery schedule reported by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
3.5 Aggregation determinations. For applications proposing new DER at sites that may host existing generation, apply the applicable aggregation provision before finalizing program-scope routing.
3.6 Capacity verifications. For any application on abnormality hold due to a stated-vs-nameplate capacity discrepancy, verify the nameplate from the application's technical documentation and apply the applicable interconnection standard to any claimed operating limit below inverter nameplate.
3.7 Hosting-capacity corrections. Before any capacity figure from the published hosting-capacity map is communicated externally, confirm that the figure reflects the current state of the affected feeder. A priority refresh is to be requested from Distribution Planning under the published refresh-prioritization criteria.
3.8 Witness-test dispositions. Verify each inverter model against the applicable certified equipment list under the commissioning procedure in effect at the time of determination. Waiver eligibility is to be determined against the applicable certified equipment list.
3.9 Supplemental-review reversals. Review any supplemental-review determination on file for consistency with current program procedures. Where the record requires revision, update the file and flag any prior memorandum that has been superseded accordingly.
4. Reporting cadence
The DER Program Manager will provide weekly progress reports to Regulatory Affairs, with copy to the VP office, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025 and continuing through 09/12/2025. The weekly report will comprise:
counts by disposition category, aligned to the categories in §3 above;
items closed on the record during the reporting week, with the governing citation named;
exceptions requiring Regulatory Affairs or VP attention, including any project at risk of missing 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025;
forward-look for the following reporting week.
Reports are to be delivered in writing. Verbal updates do not substitute.
5. General provisions
Every disposition reached under this tasking must be tariff-defensible on the face of the file. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, operating guideline, or bulletin that supports the action. Where the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready and is to be held rather than reported.
Follow the noticing, payment-deadline, and hold-clearance procedures as written. Standards or procedural conflicts route through the established referral process; they are not to be resolved informally in the queue. Queue-date treatment must remain within what the tariff and program policy permit.
Regulatory Affairs will coordinate with Interconnection Studies (Meera Vellanki) on queue and notice records, and with the DER Planning Group (Ivo Grantham) on study status, on any input required for the League response or the APUC briefing. The DER Program Manager remains the single point of accountability for the queue-cleanup inputs enumerated in §3.
Escalate obstacles to Regulatory Affairs in writing and, where the obstacle bears on the 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025 dates, to the VP office concurrently.
